articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself
articles.description: JustWatch, the popular streaming search guide used by 50 million people, is launching its own streaming service, offering free, ad-supported movies and shows alongside a $3.99-per-month ad-free tier and movie rentals.
articles.summary: JustWatch, a widely used streaming search guide with 50 million users, is expanding into the streaming market with its own ad-supported service, as well as a premium ad-free subscription option and movie rentals. The service aims to compete in a market with established players like Netflix, Amazon Prime, and Hulu.
points: JustWatch is launching its own streaming service, which will offer free, ad-supported content as well as a $3.99-per-month ad-free tier.
The service will also provide movie rentals, with content from Paramount Pictures, Sony Pictures, and NBCUniversal.
JustWatch plans to compete in the streaming market, targeting users who frequently use its streaming guide to find content.
articles.insight: JustWatch's entry into the streaming market with a robust content offering could significantly intensify the competition and compel existing streaming services to diversify their content libraries.

articles.title: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
articles.description: Electric Plant has built an AI-powered translator to help humans listen to what plants are saying with the subtle electricity coursing through their stems.
articles.summary: Electric Plant has developed an AI model to interpret the electric signals that plants emit, essentially allowing humans to 'listen' to plants. The startup's technology suggests that plants communicate through these electric signals.
points: Electric Plant, a startup founded by a team of biologists and engineers, has created an AI translator to interpret the electricity plants use to communicate.
The company'selogic AI model has the capability to convert these plant signals into understandable sounds for humans.
Electric Plant believes that plants use electricity to communicate and that they can now make it understandable for human ears.
articles.insight: This technology could revolutionize plant care and study, offering unprecedented insights into plant needs and behavior, while potentially reducing waste and inefficiencies in agricultural practices.
